h: Shabbos Raises the Soul Through Deed Speech and Heart

p: The camp of Yisrael must be
in the midst of the camp of the Shechinah and the camp of the Levites.
וּכְתִיב בְּמִזְמוֹר שֶׁל שַׁבָּת (תְּהִלִּים צב, יד)
And it is written in the psalm of Shabbos (Tehillim 92:14):
they will flourish in the courtyards of our God."
"In the House of Hashem" — the camp of the Shechinah;
"in the courtyards of our God" — the camp of the Levites,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (וַיִּקְרָא ו, ט)
along the lines of what is said (Vayikra 6:9):
"In the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting they shall eat it."
And the three camps of Yisrael
וְהוּא כְּנֶגֶד מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (דְּבָרִים ל, יד)
and this corresponds to what is said (Devarim 30:14):
"In your mouth and in your heart, to do it."
which comes through the power of the blood,
"For it is the blood that atones for the soul";
and the holiness of the nefesh
and that corresponds to the camp of the Levites,
"And you shall come to the kohanim the Levites
"And in your heart" — the camp of the Shechinah:
אֲנִי ה׳ שׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
"I am Hashem who dwells among the Children of Israel" (Bamidbar 35:34);
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב)
and as they said (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2):
שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
that HaKadosh Baruch Hu is the heart of Yisrael?
'The Rock of my heart and my portion is God,' etc."
(וְכֵן כָּתַב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קכח רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב)
(And so it is written in Zohar II 128, beginning of amud b.)
are like a candle before a torch
and the tzaddikim are the candle,
And this is what it says (Tehillim 92:13):
"The righteous shall flourish like the date palm":
for on Shabbos all Yisrael are tzaddikim,
and whoever is circumcised is called a tzaddik
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב כג, א)
and likewise Shabbos is in the secret of the bris
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק א נו, א
and all Yisrael are called tzaddik on Shabbos,
is as if he guards the entire Torah
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב פט, א)
I bring it before its time:
'Today, if you will listen to His voice,'" etc.
עַל שְׁמִירַת יוֹם אֶחָד שֶׁל שַׁבָּת
through the keeping of one day of Shabbos
for Shabbos is equal to all the mitzvos.
That is, it expounded "today" as Shabbos,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וַיֵּרָא)
(as stated in Midrash Tanchuma, beginning of parshas Vayera).
And it is written regarding Shabbos (Shemos 16:25):
for today is a Shabbos to Hashem;
today you will not find it in the field";
and from them the three Shabbos meals are derived
And one is called tzaddik in deed;
וְלָזֶה זוֹכֶה כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל בְּשַׁבָּת
and to this every one of Yisrael attains on Shabbos;
for since he guards Shabbos from profaning it,
and he is always accustomed to labors,
וַהֲוֵי כְּמוֹ בָּא לְיָדוֹ דְּבַר עֲבֵירָה
it is like when a matter of sin came into his hand
and he was saved from it,
and he is like one who does a mitzvah
"If he merits more, he merits ruach"
that is, words of Torah "in your mouth,"
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לְנֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה (בְּרֵאשִׁית ב, ז)
and as it says, "a living soul" (Bereishis 2:7),
which we translate in the Targum "a speaking spirit";
and that corresponds to the camp of the Levites, as said.
"If he merits more, he merits neshamah":
נֵר ה׳ נִשְׁמַת אָדָם (מִשְׁלֵי כ, כז)
"The candle of Hashem is the soul of man" (Mishlei 20:27),
that Hashem Yisbarach dwells in his heart;
and this is the camp of the Shechinah;
and so it is written in the holy Zohar
וּבְחֵלֶק א רו, א בְּשִׁינּוּי לָשׁוֹן)
וְאַף שֶׁבַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ מַיְירֵי בְּכָל יוֹם
And although the holy Zohar speaks of every day,
it is stated in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 20, 32b):
"And those that are added to the holy people
And although they toil in Torah on weekdays,
nevertheless they do not then merit
that every one of Yisrael merits on Shabbos,
And this is why it says "tzaddik":
דְּזֶהוּ נִקְרָא כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל בְּמַעֲשֶׂה
for so is every one of Yisrael called in deed,
and he merits the additional nefesh,
"Like the date palm shall he flourish"
that is, when he merits more,
he merits a speaking spirit in words of Torah;
and this is "like the date palm,"
for words of Torah are likened to honey,
as it says (Tehillim 19:11), "and sweeter than honey,"
"Honey and milk are under your tongue";
and the date is the honey mentioned in the Torah,
'a land of olive oil and honey.'"
"Like the date palm shall he flourish"
along the lines of what is said,
"in the courtyards of the House of our God they will flourish,"
which is the camp of the Levites,
to whom the words of Torah were given over,
"They shall teach Your judgments to Yaakov," etc.,
and "you shall come to the kohanim the Levites."
And there is the Chamber of Hewn Stone,
from which Torah goes forth to all Yisrael
for the seat of the Sanhedrin
was in the camp of the Levites,
in its half that was unconsecrated,
which has the holiness of the Temple Mount
he merits the camp of the Shechinah:
And this is what it says:
"Like a cedar in Lebanon shall he grow."
(פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, חֵלֶק ג נג סוֹף עַמּוּד א)
(on this parshah, III 53, end of amud a):
and in the gloss the Ramaz, of blessed memory, explained:
Because it whitens the sins of Yisrael";
and that is the Beis HaMikdash,
for there is the outer altar,
on which all offerings are offered,
and in the Heichal is the golden altar,
which alludes to the transgressors of Yisrael,
and into the Holy of Holies
the Kohen Gadol enters on Yom Kippur
and this is Levanon, the camp of the Shechinah.
And the cedar is the vav,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (לְקַמָּן עַמּוּד ב)
as is written in the holy Zohar (further on, amud b),
and that is Yaakov, the middle bar,
"and its saplings take root in Lebanon":
for from the union of chochmah and binah
which is the middle bar, etc.
And this is "like a cedar in Lebanon shall he grow,"
up above, up to Atika Kadisha;
גָּדוֹל אֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלֹא שִׁיעוּר
great in relation to Hashem Yisbarach, without limit
and that is because it is planted in Lebanon,
which is Abba and Imma, chochmah and binah,
that it corresponds to "in your heart":
and chochmah and binah are two companions
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג ד, א)
and therefore when one merits binah
and this is what the Ramaz wrote,
that Levanon is lamed-beis and nun,
chochmah and binah, Abba and Imma;
and it is all one, as said.

paragraphs.text: Source: Chagigah 13a — “… לן) [ליגמרן] מר מעשה מרכבה. אמר להו: אגמרון לי מעשה בראשית. בתר דאגמרוה, אמרו ליה: ליגמרון מר במעשה מרכבה! אמר להו: תנינא בהו ״דבש וחלב תחת לשונך״, דברים המתוקין מדבש …” (Oz Vehadar print, p. 206) — “The Gemara relates: Rav Yosef would study the Design of the Divine Chariot and was familiar with the subject, whereas the Elders of Pumbedita would study the act of Creation. They said to Rav Yosef: Let the Master teach us …”

paragraphs.text: Source: Devarim 8:8 — “ארץ חטה ושערה וגפן ותאנה ורמון ארץ זית שמן ודבש” — “a land of wheat and barley, of vines, figs, and pomegranates, a land of olive trees and honey;”

rich.text: “ארץ חטה ושערה וגפן ותאנה ורמון ארץ זית שמן ודבש”
— “a land of wheat and barley, of vines, figs, and pomegranates, a land of olive trees and honey;”

paragraphs.text: Source: Yoma 25a — “אמר אביי: שמע מינה לשכת הגזית חציה בקדש וחציה בחול, ושמע מינה שני פתחים היו לה, אחד פתוח בקדש, ואחד פתוח בחול. דאי סלקא דעתך כולה בקדש — זקן יושב …” (Oz Vehadar print, p. 59) — “Apropos the baraita that was just cited, Abaye said: Conclude from this baraita that the Chamber of Hewn Stone was built half in the sacred area, within the consecrated Temple grounds, and half in the non-sacred part of the Temple …”

rich.text: “אמר אביי: שמע מינה לשכת הגזית חציה בקדש וחציה בחול, ושמע מינה שני פתחים היו לה, אחד פתוח בקדש, ואחד פתוח בחול. דאי סלקא דעתך כולה בקדש — זקן יושב …”

paragraphs.text: Source: Tikkunei Zohar 285:4 — “קם רבי שמעון על רגלוי, וסליק ידוי לגבי עילא, ושבח למארי עלמא, ואמר, רבון עלמא עביד בגין שכינתא דאיהי בגלותא, ואם איהי באומאה הא אבא ואמא דאינון חכמה ובינה יכלין …”

paragraphs.text: Source: Yoma 39b — “אמר רבי יצחק בן טבלאי: למה נקרא שמו לבנון — שמלבין עונותיהן של ישראל.” (Oz Vehadar print, p. 88) — “Rabbi Yitzḥak ben Tavlai said: Why is the Temple called Lebanon [Levanon]? Because it whitens [malbin] the Jewish people’s sins, alluded to by the root lavan, meaning white.”

rich.text: “אמר רבי יצחק בן טבלאי: למה נקרא שמו לבנון — שמלבין עונותיהן של ישראל.”
— “Rabbi Yitzḥak ben Tavlai said: Why is the Temple called Lebanon [Levanon]? Because it whitens [malbin] the Jewish people’s sins, alluded to by the root lavan, meaning white.”
